citations.relevance: Supplies the referenced throughout NFPA 13 sprinkler-system requirement under BC 903.3.1.1.

controllingProvisions.label: BC 1019.3 — baseline enclosure requirement
controllingProvisions.summary: For occupancies other than Groups H, I-2, and I-3, exit access stairways or ramps must be enclosed in a shaft enclosure complying with Section 713, unless an applicable exception permits otherwise.

controllingProvisions.label: BC 1019.3, Exception 2 — limited two-story unenclosed stair exception
controllingProvisions.summary: An unenclosed exit access stairway may serve only the first and second stories above grade when the building is equipped throughout with an automatic sprinkler system under Section 903.3.1.1; both stories must have the required independent exits, never fewer than two means of egress; the interconnected stories may not be open to other stories; and the stairway must be remotely located under Section 1007.

controllingProvisions.label: BC 1019.3, Exception 4 — draft-curtain/opening exception
controllingProvisions.summary: A draft curtain is one required element of a separate exception allowing an exit access stairway or ramp where the building is sprinklered throughout, the vertical opening is no more than twice the stair or ramp's horizontal projected area, and closely spaced sprinklers are provided in accordance with NFPA 13 as modified by Appendix Q. For occupancies other than Groups B and M, the provision is limited to openings connecting no more than four stories.

generalRules.label: Sprinkler-system reference
generalRules.summary: Where the code requires a building or portion thereof to be equipped throughout with an automatic sprinkler system under Section 903.3.1.1, sprinklers are to be installed throughout in accordance with NFPA 13, subject to the stated code exceptions.

exceptions.label: Exception 2 is not satisfied by a draft curtain alone
exceptions.summary: The supplied text places the draft-curtain requirement in Exception 4, not Exception 2. Exception 2 instead requires a sprinklered building, service limited to the first and second stories above grade, required independent exits on both stories, at least two means of egress, no opening to other stories, and remote location under Section 1007.

conditions.label: Conditions for Exception 2
conditions.summary: The project must establish all of the following: occupancy other than H, I-2, or I-3; automatic sprinkler protection throughout under Section 903.3.1.1; the stair serving only the first and second stories above grade; the required independent exits for both stories and at least two means of egress; no openness of those interconnected stories to other stories; and remote location under Section 1007.

conditions.label: Conditions for Exception 4
conditions.summary: The project must establish sprinkler protection throughout, a vertical opening no larger than twice the stairway's horizontal projected area, a draft curtain, closely spaced NFPA 13 sprinklers as modified by Appendix Q, and—outside Groups B and M—an opening connecting no more than four stories.

conditions.label: Independent-exit condition referenced by Exception 2
conditions.summary: The supplied evidence cross-references Section 1006 requirements for the minimum number of approved independent exits. The available Table 1006.3.2 evidence contains different permitted occupant-load and travel-distance values by story and occupancy; the applicable row depends on the project's actual occupancy, story, sprinkler status, and other listed qualifiers.

limitations.label: Material project facts are unresolved
limitations.summary: The supplied project facts do not establish occupancy, sprinkler status, stories connected, whether each story has the required independent exits, whether the stories are open to other stories, or whether the stair is remotely located. Those facts can materially change the conclusion.

limitations.label: Draft curtain does not establish applicability of Exception 2
limitations.summary: The proposal is described as relying on Exception 2 with a draft curtain, but the supplied enacted text supports the draft-curtain condition under Exception 4. The proposal therefore identifies the wrong exception unless the project independently satisfies Exception 2 or is analyzed under Exception 4.

limitations.label: Bounded evidence package
limitations.summary: This map is limited to the supplied 2022 NYC Construction Codes evidence. The package states that eight enacted sections were unavailable from the canonical resolver, at least one section was shortened, one large definitions section was represented only by a targeted excerpt, additional direct cross-references were not added, and lexical retrieval may miss differently worded requirements.

definitions.label: Relevant egress terms
definitions.summary: The supplied definitions identify an exit access stairway as a stairway within the exit-access portion of the means-of-egress system, and define exit access as the portion leading from an occupied portion of the building to an exit.

crossReferences.label: BC 903.3.1.1
crossReferences.summary: Referenced by both principal exceptions for the required throughout sprinkler system; the supplied text requires NFPA 13 installation throughout, subject to stated exceptions.

crossReferences.label: BC 1006
crossReferences.summary: Referenced by Exception 2 for the minimum number of approved independent exits. The supplied Table 1006.3.2 provides occupancy- and story-specific single-exit limits, but does not resolve the project's applicable row without the missing project facts.

crossReferences.label: BC 1007
crossReferences.summary: Referenced by Exception 2 for the required remote location of unenclosed exit access stairways and ramps. The supplied package does not include the text of Section 1007.

crossReferences.label: NFPA 13 as modified by Appendix Q
crossReferences.summary: Referenced by Exception 4 for closely spaced sprinklers protecting the opening. The supplied package does not include the detailed Appendix Q or NFPA 13 provisions governing that protection.

tables.label: BC Table 1006.3.2 — alternative occupancy/story rows
tables.summary: The table places materially different categories and limits in separate rows. For example, on the second story above grade, Groups B, F, M, and S have a maximum occupant load of 29 and 75 feet maximum travel distance, while R-2 has NA occupant load and 50 feet maximum travel distance. The applicable category is selected by the project's actual occupancy; the R-2 alternative cannot be applied without an established R-2 fact.

AUTOMATIC SPRINKLER SYSTEM. A fire suppression or control device that operates automatically when its heat-activated element is heated to its thermal rating or above, allowing water to discharge over a specified area. DWELLING UNIT. A single unit consisting of one or more habitable rooms and occupied or arranged to be occupied as a unit separate from all other units within a dwelling. EXIT ACCESS. That portion of a means of egress system that leads from any occupied portion of a building or structure to an exit. EXIT ACCESS STAIRWAY. A stairway within the exit access portion of the means of egress system. MEANS OF EGRESS. A continuous and unobstructed path of vertical and horizontal egress travel from any occupied portion of a building or structure to a public way. A means of egress consists of three separate and distinct parts: the exit access, the exit and the exit discharge. OPEN PARKING GARAGE . A structure or portion of a structure with the openings as described in Section 406 . 5 . 2 that is used for the parking or storage of private motor vehicles as described in Section 406 . 5.3 . The walls or construction forming the boundaries of a shaft.

1009.3 1009.3 Exit stairways. To be considered part of an accessible means of egress, a stairway between stories shall have a clear width of 48 inches (1220 mm) minimum between handrails and shall either incorporate an area of rescue assistance within an enlarged floor-level landing or shall be accessed from an area of rescue assistance complying with Section 1009.6. Exit access stairways that connect levels in the same story are not permitted as part of an accessible means of egress. Exceptions: The following exceptions apply to the requirements of clear width and area of rescue assistance, and do not supersede the other requirements of the accessible means of egress: 1. Exit access stairways providing means of egress from mezzanines are permitted as part of an accessible means of egress. 2. The clear width of 48 inches (1220 mm) between handrails and the area of rescue assistance is not required at exit access stairways as permitted by Section 1017 or exit stairways in buildings equipped throughout with an automatic sprinkler system installed in accordance with Section 903.3.1.1 or 903.3.1.2. 3. The clear width of 48 inches (1220 mm) between handrails is not required for interior exit stairways accessed from a refuge area in conjunction with a horizontal exit. 4. Areas of rescue assistance are not required at exit access stairways where two-way communication is provided at the elevator landing in accordance with Section 1009.8. 5. Areas of rescue assistance are not required at stairways in buildings equipped throughout with an automatic sprinkler system installed in accordance with Section 903.3.1.1 or 903.3.1.2. 6. Areas of rescue assistance are not required at stairways serving open parking garages. 7. Areas of rescue assistance are not required for smoke-protected assembly seating areas complying with Section 1029.6.2. 8. Areas of rescue assistance are not required in Group R-2 occupancies. 9. Areas of rescue assistance are not required for stairways accessed from a refuge area in conjunction with a horizontal exit.

1006.3 1006.3 Egress from stories or occupied roofs. The means of egress system serving any story, or occupied roof designed for human occupancy or use, shall be provided with the number of exits or access to exits based on the aggregate occupant load served in accordance with this section. The path of egress travel to an exit shall not pass through more than one adjacent story. Each story or occupied roof designed for human occupancy or use above the second story of a building shall have not less than one interior or exterior exit stairway, or interior or exterior exit ramp. Where three or more exits or access to exits are required, not less than 50 percent of the required exits shall be interior or exterior exit stairways or ramps. Exceptions: 1. Interior exit stairways and interior exit ramps are not required in open parking garages where the means of egress serves only the open parking garage. 2. Interior exit stairways and interior exit ramps are not required in outdoor facilities where all portions of the means of egress are essentially open to the outside.

903.2.11.3 903.2.11.3 Other below-grade stories. An automatic sprinkler system shall be installed throughout every first basement or cellar story below grade of buildings on which access is not provided directly from the outdoors within each 100 feet (30 480 mm) or fraction thereof of horizontal length of every wall that fronts on a street or frontage space required pursuant to Section 501.3.1. Exceptions: 1. One- and two-family dwellings need not provide direct access. 2. Any building classified in Occupancy Group R-2 not more than three stories in height and with not more than two dwelling units on any story need not provide direct access when such first basement or cellar story is used for dwelling units or for uses accessory to the residential use in the building. 3. Except as provided in Exception 2, above, for Group R-1 and R-2 occupancies, only one direct access from the outdoors to the first basement or cellar story consisting of a stair or door shall be required when such story is used for dwelling units or for uses accessory to the residential use in the building.

1006.3.2.1 1006.3.2.1 Mixed occupancies. Where one exit, or exit access stairway or ramp providing access to exits at other stories, is permitted to serve individual stories, mixed occupancies shall be permitted to be served by single exits provided each individual occupancy complies with the applicable requirements of Table 1006.3.2 for that occupancy. Where applicable, cumulative occupant loads from adjacent occupancies shall be considered in accordance with the provisions of Section 1004.1. In each story of a mixed occupancy building, the maximum number of occupants served by a single exit shall be such that the sum of the ratios of the calculated number of occupants of the space divided by the allowable number of occupants indicated in Table 1006.3.2 for each occupancy does not exceed one. Where dwelling units are located on a story with other occupancies, the actual number of dwelling units divided by four plus the ratio from the other occupancy does not exceed one.

3006.1.1 3006.1.1 Elevator lobby. Except as provided by Sections 403.6.1 and 403.6.2, an enclosed elevator lobby shall be provided in high-rise buildings at the following locations: 1. Elevators opening onto a fire-resistance-rated corridor, in all occupancy groups. 2. Elevators serving Group B occupancies. Elevators that serve four or more stories that contain space classified in occupancy Group B, inclusive of any lobby or entrance level, shall provide elevator lobbies at every level served by such elevator. The lobby enclosure shall separate the elevator shaft enclosure doors from each floor by smoke partitions. In addition to the requirements in Section 710 for smoke partitions, doors protecting openings in the elevator lobby enclosure walls shall also comply with Section 710.5.2.3 and penetrations of the elevator lobby enclosure by ducts and air transfer openings shall be protected in accordance with Section 710.8. Elevator lobbies shall have at least one means of egress complying with Chapter 10 and other provisions within this code. Access to an exit on any story through an elevator lobby shall be permitted provided that access to at least one other required exit does not require passing through the elevator lobby. Exceptions: 1. Enclosed elevator lobbies are not required at the street floor, provided the entire street floor is equipped with an automatic sprinkler system in accordance with Section 903.3.1.1. 2. Elevators not required to be located in a shaft in accordance with Section 712 are not required to have enclosed elevator lobbies. 3. Enclosed elevator lobbies are not required where zero-clearance doors are provided at the hoistway opening in accordance with Section 3002.6. Such doors shall be tested in accordance with UL 1784 without an artificial bottom seal. 4. Enclosed elevator lobbies are not required on floors with less than 2,500 square feet (232 m 2 ), provided that the commissioner accepts an alternative design or construction method that accomplishes the purposes of this section, or provided that the commissioner determines that compliance with this section is impracticable in whole or in part, whereby the commissioner may authorize an exemption from the requirements of this section. 5. Enclosed elevator lobbies are not required on Group R-2 occupied floors. 6. Enclosed elevator lobbies are not required where the elevator hoistway is pressurized in accordance with Section 3006.1.2. 7. Enclosed elevator lobbies are not required where the elevator serves only open parking garages in accordance with Section 406.5.
